newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea police fire tear gas at student protesters.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea police fire tear gas at student protesters.

text.p: Police helicopters firing teargas flew low over hundreds of students at a Seoul university campus on Friday as the students tried to stage an anti-government rally, eyewitnesses said.
More than 500 students shouted anti-government slogans in small groups, but failed to launch a massed rally after police helicopters swooped down.
They shouted slogans such as "Down With the Kim Young-sam Government" and "Apologise for Suppression of Student Movements" in several parts of the Seoul National University campus in southern Seoul.
No casualties were witnessed or reported.
The students demanded an official apology for what they call "an excessive repression of protesting students" in August at another university campus.
On August 20, South Korean riot police supported by helicopters stormed the Yonsei University campus to end a seven-day occupation by students demanding reunification with North Korea.
